title: A complete parity classification
summary: For every n >= 0, a(n) is odd exactly when n modulo 10 is 1, 3, 7, or 9. Every a(2n) is even. For n >= 1, a(2n-1) is even if and only if n=5k-2 for some k >= 1.
qualifications: Source offset zero. The proof concerns the actual third composition and gives every n >= 0. Both source assertions and the stronger complete parity pattern are included.

title: Cubic reversion modulo nine and three
summary: The normalized integral source solution is unique. Its square is congruent to x^2+2x^3 modulo 9. For all n,k >= 0, the coefficient of A(x)^(3k)-A(x^3)^k is zero modulo 3.
qualifications: Source offset one. Integral construction, source uniqueness, and genuine compositional inversion are proved. The modulo-three power assertion is a standard Frobenius consequence, not a new general mathematical principle.

title: Two cubic congruences in characteristic three
summary: The normalized integral source solution is unique. As full formal series, A(x)^3 is congruent to A(x^3), and A(x)^2 is congruent to x^2+2A(x^3), modulo 3.
qualifications: Source offset one. Integral construction and source uniqueness are proved. The cube identity is standard Frobenius; the square identity additionally uses the defining equation. Both identities hold at every coefficient index.

title: Congruences for an inverse-iterate family
summary: The equation A(A(A(x)))=(1+x)A(A(x)) has a unique normalized integral solution. Every positive-index coefficient is 1 modulo 3. The coefficient at index n of the kth natural iterate is k^(n-1) modulo 3. The full parameter family is included.
qualifications: Source offset one. A396102 is F_3; the original-family existence theorem uses parameter r+1, so r=2 gives its triple equation. All natural iterates and the general positive-parameter family are included. Formal ZMod 0 extensions are not needed for the stated positive-modulus result.

title: Catalan-weighted Stirling periodicity
summary: For every m >= 1 and n >= m, a(n+φ(m)) is congruent to a(n) modulo m. The least positive period of the tail beginning at m exists and divides φ(m); positivity, minimality, and periodicity are all formalized.
qualifications: Known result, credited to Payam Danesh and earlier related Fubini-periodicity work. Source offset zero. Lean proves the explicit finite Stirling sum with the exact integer weight, the totient period, and the least-tail-period properties. The EGF substitution identity is explained and proved in the manuscript but is not separately a Lean theorem. The onset n >= m is sufficient; optimality is not asserted. The stronger Carmichael-period bound is not formalized here.
